stories.notes: Story has no acceptance criteria and no existing spec. It is a multi-brand (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature for the CMS, which is inherently complex with real-time rendering, cross-platform concerns, and security considerations. Openspec must first elaborate ACs, propose story splits, and add technical depth; speckit then hardens with testability criteria, edge cases, and security checks.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new capability (Live Preview) that does not exist in the codebase. ContentstackProvider currently passes only static defaultContent with no preview token, host, or live-update mechanism. All 236 useContent callers depend on this provider. This is novel work, not a defect. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. Contentstack API is unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our side of the boundary.

Openspec provided empty ACs with a helpful note that this is novel work. I authored all 15 criteria from scratch based on the story title, description, and openspec's analysis of the current codebase (static defaultContent only, no preview token/host/update mechanism, 236 useContent callers, 3 sites). Key areas covered: (1) core preview vs published behavior (AC-1, AC-2), (2) live real-time updates (AC-3), (3) error/fallback handling for invalid tokens, unreachable hosts, and missing drafts (AC-5, AC-6, AC-9), (4) connection interruption resilience (AC-4), (5) security — no preview secrets in production bundles (AC-7), (6) backward compatibility with existing callers (AC-10), (7) multi-site consistency (AC-11), (8) preview context persistence and cleanup (AC-8, AC-12, AC-15), (9) concurrent update handling (AC-13), (10) ContentstackLink preview support (AC-14). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual file contents of ContentstackContext.tsx, useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx. The internal structure of the provider and hook may affect the granularity and feasibility of some criteria. Once file contents are reviewed, AC-14 (ContentstackLink) and AC-13 (concurrent updates) may need adjustment based on the actual update mechanism chosen.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec analyzed the codebase (236 useContent callers, no existing preview token/host/update mechanism, static defaultContent only) and derived 3 verification criteria from the description. Speckit then authored 15 acceptance criteria covering security (no preview secrets in production bundles), error/fallback handling, connection resilience, backward compatibility, multi-site consistency, concurrent updates, and ContentstackLink preview support — substantial hardening work that does not overlap openspec's analysis. The 3 verificationCriteria are observable and testable: (1) draft content displays in preview mode, (2) live updates without manual refresh, (3) all content reflects preview state. File set is plausible: context manages preview state, hook fetches with preview parameters, interface defines content types, link component needs preview support. All 4 manifest paths confirmed EXISTS. CROSS-CODELINE PATH VARIANCE (resolved but writer must be aware): upexpress declares src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx but actual file is src/context/ContentstackContext.ts (extension_variant — .tsx vs .ts); metrolinx declares ContentstackContext.tsx but actual is contentstackContext.tsx (case_variant — lowercase 'c'). gotransit has exact matches for all 4. Speckit's caveat about not having file contents is noted but per policy does not lower the score. Empty acceptanceCriteria and acceptanceChanged=false are expected for brownfield per redaction policy.
